passage: Zubin, you think I was always disciplined? Your Kishore Chacha hated chemistry practice at your age. Balancing equations, page after page. I'd open the book, feel bored, and find ten other things to do. One evening I thought, "The problem isn't that it's hard. It's that it has no end. I keep putting it off because it feels endless." So I took Amma's kitchen timer, the round one, and set it for twenty-five minutes. "Just until it rings. Then I'm free." Twenty-five minutes felt small enough to start. By the time it rang, I'd done twelve equations. I did one timer every day. Endless tasks, beta, you cut them into pieces you can see the end of.

qa.q: What did young Kishore set the timer for?
What did young Kishore realise about why he avoided chemistry?
qa.a: Young Kishore realised the boredom and putting off came because the practice felt endless, not because it was hard.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Setting a twenty-five-minute timer, because a short, bounded start was easy to begin and ended at a clear point.

qa.q: How might Kishore's Amma have seen him using her kitchen timer?
qa.a: She might have been amused and pleased to see him finally sitting down with chemistry.

passage: The chemistry test was on Monday, and on Sunday afternoon Francis's family had guests, the house full of noise and cousins. He'd been avoiding the practice sheet all weekend. It wasn't hard, just boring and long. He thought, "If I wait for a quiet, free evening, it won't come. I'll never feel like doing this." His friend Karthik had mentioned a trick: set a timer, just twenty-five minutes. Francis took his phone and the sheet to the terrace, where it was quieter. "Twenty-five minutes, then I can go back down." He set it and started. The cousins' shouting drifted up. When the timer rang, he had finished half the sheet. He set it once more after tea, and finished.

qa.q: Where did Francis take the practice sheet?
qa.a: To the terrace, where it was quieter.

qa.q: How did Francis feel about the practice sheet before using the timer?
qa.a: He felt bored and reluctant, sure he would never feel like doing it.

qa.q: Why did a timer suit this task?
qa.a: The sheet was dull and easy to postpone, so a short, bounded block made starting easy even in a noisy house.

qa.q: How might Karthik feel hearing the trick worked?
qa.a: Karthik would likely feel pleased his idea helped Francis finish before the test.
